issue: The outcome box collapses distinct candidate statuses and host requirements: it labels (a) and (b) 'SURVIVORS' and says 'each needs a ~5-host prefill pool', while the caption says all three are conditional with open gates and Table 12-1 says (b) is a conditional finalist needing a ~5-host prefill pool plus a decode pool and fabric, and (a) is not a P/D-disaggregated prefill pool.
evidence: Figure text: 'SURVIVORS (a) · (b) each needs a ~5-host prefill pool'; caption: 'three conditional candidates, each with its own open validation gate (not a settled verdict)'; Table 12-1 row (b): 'conditional finalist — X throughput at a single prefill host ... prefill pool must itself scale to ~5 hosts ... plus a decode pool; ~2× capex plus fabric'.
acceptance_test: Revise the outcome box to show (a) conditional finalist / homogeneous ~5-host serving pool; (b) conditional finalist / ~5-host prefill pool + decode pool + fabric; (c) gated pending Ch. 14; or remove host counts and refer to Table 12-1. Do not use 'SURVIVORS' as a settled verdict unless the caption and table use the same status.

issue: Green is used for two different meanings: the downward triangles under each tier say 'constraints → STOP' (do not escalate), while the right-hand dashed arrow says 'DE-ESCALATE: privacy · cost' (move down a tier). Both are green and point downward, so the figure visually conflates 'stop escalating' with 'de-escalate'.
evidence: Figure labels: green triangles 'constraints → STOP' under Single GPU/Single host/Multi-host/Cluster/fleet; green dashed arrow 'DE-ESCALATE: privacy · cost'; caption: 'de-escalation (green) fires on privacy, data sovereignty, and cost'.
acceptance_test: Use distinct encodings: e.g., gray stop bars for 'no binding constraint → stay at tier' and reserve green for de-escalation; or relabel the triangles 'no binding constraint → stay' and add a legend. Ensure the caption and figure use the same term for each action.

issue: The bottom caveat 'escalate only when a constraint binds — else STOP; tiers are orthogonal levels of scale, not a ranking' is set in small, light-gray type. It carries an important semantic qualification (the ladder is not a quality ranking) but is likely to be missed or hard to read at print size.
evidence: Rendered page shows the note in light gray below the diagram, smaller and lower contrast than the box labels; the caption repeats the ranking caveat only indirectly.
acceptance_test: Darken the note to at least 70% black and set it at or above the 8 pt print floor, or move the caveat into the caption/body text. Verify at 100% print size and in grayscale.

issue: The note says 'tiers are orthogonal levels of scale, not a ranking'. Levels of scale are nested/ordered, not orthogonal; 'orthogonal' suggests independent dimensions and conflicts with the ladder's vertical ordering.
evidence: Figure note: 'tiers are orthogonal levels of scale, not a ranking'; the diagram itself draws a single vertical escalation ladder from Single GPU to Cluster/fleet.
acceptance_test: Replace 'orthogonal levels of scale' with 'nested levels of scale' or 'different scales, not a quality ranking' in the figure and caption. Ensure 'orthogonal' is not used for nested tiers.

issue: The capability-screen box is labeled 'Capability MMLU/GSM8K' without an 'e.g.' or scope qualifier. This can imply that MMLU/GSM8K are sufficient capability screens, while §14.7 says capability benchmarks may not predict enterprise Q&A quality and a custom retrieval-QA screen is stronger.
evidence: Figure text: 'Capability MMLU/GSM8K'; caption: '[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]'; §14.7: 'How closely capability benchmarks predict enterprise Q&A quality ... is [UNRESOLVED]; a custom retrieval-QA screen on real documents is stronger but costly.'
acceptance_test: Change the label to 'Capability screen (e.g., MMLU/GSM8K, domain eval)' or 'Capability screen (task-specific eval)' and add a caption note that MMLU/GSM8K are illustrative examples, not a sufficient screen. Ensure the figure does not contradict §14.7.

issue: The BEFORE panel labels the baseline 'naive / SDPA', and the caption says 'Before (naive / SDPA), the intermediate attention matrix is materialized to HBM and re-read'. SDPA is the scaled-dot-product attention operation, not a particular materialized implementation; fused SDPA kernels (including FlashAttention) implement the same operation without materializing the full matrix. The label conflates the mathematical operation with a naive implementation.
evidence: Figure label: 'BEFORE: naive / SDPA'; caption: 'Before (naive / SDPA), the intermediate attention matrix is materialized to HBM and re-read'; page 227 text defines SDPA as 'Scaled-dot-product attention (SDPA)' and discusses FlashAttention as an implementation of the same math.
acceptance_test: Relabel the panel 'BEFORE: naive materialized attention' and revise the caption to 'a naive materialized implementation (not SDPA as an API)'. If 'SDPA' is retained, define it explicitly as the mathematical operation and distinguish it from a materialized kernel.

issue: The BEFORE annotation says 'O(L²) HBM traffic: every query re-reads the K/V row-block'. This attributes the O(L²) traffic to K/V re-reads and omits the L×L attention matrix that the caption says is materialized to HBM and re-read. The figure's arrows show only on-chip↔HBM traffic, not the intermediate matrix, so the main source of the O(L²) traffic is visually absent.
evidence: Figure red text: 'O(L²) HBM traffic: every query re-reads the K/V row-block'; caption: 'the intermediate attention matrix is materialized to HBM and re-read, so every query block re-streams the full K/V row-block'; AFTER panel: 'no L×L intermediate at HBM'.
acceptance_test: Revise the BEFORE annotation to name both sources: 'O(L²) HBM traffic: L×L attention matrix written/re-read; K/V also re-streamed per query block'. Add a visual element for the materialized L×L intermediate (or label the existing arrows as K/V re-streaming) so the figure's main causal claim matches the caption.

issue: The right panel plots 'Relative decode goodput (a.u.)' rising monotonically while its annotation says 'tail latency keeps rising'. Goodput is SLO-compliant throughput; if tail latency rises past the SLO, goodput should plateau or fall, not keep rising. As drawn, the curve is throughput, not goodput, and it can teach the wrong lesson that batching always improves goodput even as latency degrades.
evidence: Right panel y-axis: 'Relative decode goodput (a.u.)'; red annotation: 'diminishing gains past ~b16 (no hard plateau): goodput still rises; tail latency keeps rising'; caption: 'batching raises decode goodput ... rising until HBM bandwidth saturates'. The book elsewhere treats goodput as SLO-compliant throughput.
acceptance_test: Either relabel the y-axis 'relative decode throughput (a.u.)' and add a separate SLO-compliant goodput curve that plateaus/drops when p95/p99 SLO is breached, or define the SLO and plot goodput under that SLO. Annotate the batch size where the SLO violation begins.

issue: The left panel plots 'Prefill FLOPs / req (% of no-cache)' against 'Avg prefix reuse' but does not state the shared-prefix fraction. At x=32 the green curve is about 60% of no-cache work; if the entire prompt is repeated 32 times and the prefix is cached, per-request prefill work should be about 1/32 ≈ 3%, not 60%. The plotted curve implies roughly 41% of prefill work is in the reusable prefix, an assumption not stated.
evidence: Left panel green curve: x=1 → 100%; x=32 → ~60%. Caption: 'prefix caching cuts prefill work per repeated prompt'. The curve's shallow decline is not derivable from the stated axes without an unstated shared-prefix fraction.
acceptance_test: State the shared-prefix fraction and formula (e.g., work = (1-f) + f/R) in the caption or panel; or relabel the x-axis to 'average reusable-prefix fraction' if that is what is plotted; or redraw for a stated f (e.g., f=0.8) so the curve matches the 'repeated prompt' claim. Ensure the y-values are derivable from the stated assumptions.
